rows.medi_said: I don't know how to say cough. She has a cough.
rows.amal_said: They say but كح. I say كحة.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say cough and Amal supplied كحة.

rows.amal_said: You're worried about. You're worried from. ... Men، men.
rows.why: Worried takes من; he used لا الـ, Amal said 'You're worried from' / 'Men' and he said من نار.

rows.amal_said: no. There's another word for that.
rows.right: (another word for a fire starting; Amal put it aside, not given)
rows.why: He used يبدأ (begin) for a fire starting; Amal said no, another word is used, but did not supply it.

rows.medi_said: do I know how to say taking care or like caring for?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say taking care; Amal supplied ديرت بالي.

rows.medi_said: di- uh, ديرت بالـ ختيفتي، ختيفتي.
rows.why: دير بال takes على; Amal recast with على (and the -ي ending on بال).
rows.english: I took care of my fiancee

rows.why: He dropped على after دير بالي again ~2 min after A7; Amal named the rule ('بدير بالي takes على') and he said ديرت بالي على ختيفتي at 11:50. A separate moment: she fixed it a second time, not a GR-28 repeat (>30 s later).
rows.english: I took care of my fiancée.
rows.r3_why: Real, second voiced fix of the same rule, separate from A7.

rows.amal_said: دير بالك is actually the command form.
rows.why: For the 'take care' command he said باليك; Amal gave دير بالك (the -ak ending, no extra -i-).

rows.medi_said: الدرس إنه إنتي... / خلينا نعمل الدرس إنه، تفتتلي.
rows.why: He said twice (14:42, 15:00) 'the lesson that you planned' (his own English at 15:13) with إنه instead of اللي; Amal's كيف يعني؟ was about تفتتلي (A10), not the relative word, so she let it pass.
rows.english: Let's do the lesson that you planned.
rows.r3_why: Real relative-clause slip she did not address.

rows.why: After خلينا the verb is a bare present; he used the past عملنا, Amal said نعمل and he repeated it.

rows.right: خططتيلي (B reading; sheet: i planned | Ana 5a66atet | أنا خططت)
rows.why: Non-word for 'you planned for me'; Amal only asked what he meant and never supplied the word (my reading from the sheet's خطط).
rows.english: the lesson that you planned for me

rows.why: He could not recall sky (guessed أسف = عصفور, 'No. That's bird'); Amal supplied سما. Sheet: 'sky | Sama | سما'.
rows.r3_why: Didn't-know, Amal supplied the word; absorbs D3.

rows.medi_said: When, when do you look at the sky? When do you watch the sky?
rows.amal_said: No، امتى بتتطلع على الشمس would be when do you watch the sky؟ امتى الشمس بتطلع؟ ... When does the sun go up؟
rows.why: He understood her امتى الشمس بتطلع as 'when do you watch the sky'; Amal said no, it is 'when does the sun go up'.
rows.r3_challenge: Not a speaking slip: he mistranslated Amal's question امتى الشمس بتطلع؟ as 'when do you watch the sky?' - he misread her Arabic, so it should be mode = listening (kept apart), not a speaking vocab-A.

rows.medi_said: Is it Azan? ... بس سجر. سجر؟
rows.amal_said: أذان؟ No. أذان is the call to prayer. فجر.
rows.why: He guessed أذان for dawn (as a question), Amal said no and supplied فجر; his سجر is the same word with a sound slip (S4).
تلك is MSA, not Levantine (هاي / هديك); she let it pass. My reading.
He added لو to غير (other than); Amal said 'No لو. غير' and explained لو belongs to حتى لو.
غير never takes el- on the next noun; Amal recast غير شمس و يوم and repeated it at 20:30 when he asked.
rows.english: other than the sun and clouds

rows.medi_said: بس في الـ، الـ، الليل سما. في الليل سما
rows.why: The sky needs el- and comes first; Amal recast السما بالليل and he repeated الـ سما بي الليل.

rows.medi_said: الـ سما بي الليل بي قمر. الـ قمر. الـ قمر.
rows.why: After في (there is) the new noun takes no el-; he first said بي قمر (right) then switched to الـ قمر; Amal said قمر twice over him but he kept الـ قمر at 22:09 - unclear if her قمر was a recast or an echo of 22:03, so B / low.
rows.english: In the sky at night there is a moon.
rows.r3_why: Existential في takes an indefinite noun; Amal's قمر may be a recast but it is not clear, so grammar-B low.

rows.why: Didn't-know: he forgot the word for dark; Amal supplied عتمة.
'One' goes after the noun (شمس وحدة); Amal let it pass with 'Great job'.
rows.r3_challenge: Amal accepted واحدة شمس ('Mm-hmm. واحدة. Great job.') - fine as grammar-B, but she clearly did not correct it; check it is never scored as a voiced fix.

rows.why: نجمة is feminine so the adjective is تانية; Amal echoed تاني back and he fixed it to تانية, she said مهم.
Amal prompted the pointer ending and he said بشوفها ('I forgot the pointer').
rows.english: This is the first star I see today

rows.medi_said: since is لـ-لـ-lessa, right? ... Is it لا؟
rows.amal_said: No. Since-- لا is until. ... من.
rows.why: Didn't-know asked as guesses: لسه, then لا (until); Amal said no and supplied من.
Past 'it rained' (feminine) is مطرت; Amal recast and he repeated 'Matarat'.

rows.medi_said: آآ، بيد من because it's comparative, right?
rows.why: 'Different' takes عن not من; Amal said عن (engine wrote زعلتكش عن) and he took it ('بيد always takes and').

rows.amal_said: آخر المرة means the last of the time. The end of the time. ... آخر مرة. The last time.
rows.why: آخر + el- = the end of; 'the last time' is آخر مرة with no el-.
مرة is feminine so كانت; Amal prompted 'مرة is' and he said كانت.

rows.amal_said: No. ثلاث سنين الماضيين أو الماضيات would be for the last three years. ... Ago is قبل. So قبل ثلاث سنين.
rows.why: He used الماضي (past/last) for 'ago'; Amal said no, ago is قبل.

rows.medi_said: Il hawa aju ktir il sabah
rows.amal_said: إيش يعني عجل؟ ... عجا كتير الصباح؟ إيش يعني؟ ... Tell me it was very strong. The wind was very strong in the mornings.
rows.why: Engine wrote aju; Amal's echo عجا كتير shows he said aja (singular), so no number slip. The error is the wrong verb: اجا (came) for the wind being strong; she did not understand ('إيش يعني') and gave the English rephrase 'it was very strong'; he then said il hawa kaan awi ktir.
rows.english: The wind was very strong this morning.
rows.r3_why: Trust Amal's echo عجا (singular), so not B18; the fix she voiced is the word choice -> vocab-A tier 1.

rows.medi_said: El nar, nar heret me. Does that count correct?
rows.why: 'Me' rides on the verb as -ني; he said 'heret me', Amal recast حرقتني.
The object 'it' (the floor) rides on the verb; Amal prompted 'It.' and he said Nadabet ha, she recast نظفتها.

rows.medi_said: Is it bee? Is it bee plants? ... what's the bee?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the word for plants; Amal supplied زريعة.
Didn't-know: he could not recall stone; Amal supplied حجر.

rows.why: Amal asked 'طيب rocks', he said ما بعرف, and she supplied صخر. Sheet: 'rock | Sa5ra | صخرة'.
He meant 'the streets' (plural) but said the singular with a feminine adjective; Amal recast الشوارع and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: Or just حجر. Are stone. ... Made of is different than made.
rows.why: No verb needed for 'are (made of) stone'; Amal dropped عملت: الشوارع ... حجر.
rows.english: The streets in Amsterdam are stone

rows.amal_said: تاني حجر or الحجر التاني. You said it first right.
rows.why: حجر تاني means 'another stone'; for 'the second stone' it is تاني حجر or الحجر التاني.

rows.amal_said: So you could either say my favorite stone or my favorite using عندي. المفضل عندي.
rows.why: 'My favorite' alone is المفضل عندي (el- + عندي), not مفضل لي.

rows.medi_said: I was gonna say الـ مفضل حجر.
rows.amal_said: الحجر المفضل or حجري المفضل. المفضل is an adjective.
rows.why: The adjective goes after the noun; Amal named it.
A noun with a possessive ending never takes el-; Amal: 'No ال first'.

rows.amal_said: But al-mufaddal is an adjective, so it follows ders. ... هاد الدرس المفضل عندي.
rows.why: Standing alone 'my favorite' needs el-: المفضل عندي; Amal explained it is an adjective following الدرس.

rows.amal_said: مش هون. مش، مش في. مش هون. ... في is not is. في is there is.
rows.why: He used في (there is) as the verb 'is' in 'his favorite book isn't here'; Amal named the rule 'في is not is, في is there is' - Arabic needs no 'to be': just مش هون. He took it ('مش هون. Okay, you're right').
rows.r3_why: Amal named a grammar rule (no word for 'is'), so grammar C1, not vocab.
